visual_language.line_and_value: Retain strong mature fictional-adult character design while testing clean graphic, ink-and-gouache, clear-line watercolor, and flatter cel-painted treatments.
visual_language.density_rule: Use density as chapter rhythm, not a constant quality proxy. Dense hero/action anchors alternate with lower-density dialogue, deduction, orientation, and transition panels.
visual_language.motion_rule: Prefer causal physical action—footfall, cloth lift, mud, leverage, smoke, taut objects, or weight shift—over generic speed-line texture.
visual_language.lettering_rule: No opaque lettering may cover a person or face. Conditional overlap is allowed only when transparency preserves facial expression, silhouette, causal hands/props, and phone-size readability.
visual_language.quality_rule: Judge role identity, blocking, story-object causality, silhouette, face/hand integrity, and lettering clearance separately from surface polish.

panel_cadence.wide_action_anchor: Use landscape width for directional travel, pursuit, reveals, and geography; keep one quiet sky or wall field.
panel_cadence.tall_practical_action: Use portrait height for reach, fall, climb, leverage, shafts, and vertical architecture; causal geometry must remain fully visible.
panel_cadence.medium_character_beat: Use medium portrait or near-square framing for deduction and dialogue; preserve a face-safe quiet field.
panel_cadence.small_insert: Use compact inserts for hands, map, twine, tracks, tin, and other story objects when a full character panel would add density without information.
panel_cadence.size_boundary: Panel size is a comic-layout decision linked to ComicPanelPlan narrative function, not an AnimationShotPlan or E-Conte record.
